324243.stmt:
Let $K$ be the global function field in the paper's setting. For every finite extension $L/K$, every integer $r\geq 1$, every Drinfeld module $\phi/L$ of rank $r$, and every non-torsion point $x\in\phi(L)$, write $\hat{h}_\phi(x)$ for the canonical height, $h(j_\phi)$ for the height of its $j$-invariant, and $\deg(\mathscr{D}_{\phi/L})$ for the degree of its discriminant divisor. **Lang–Silverman conjecture.** For every finite extension $L/K$ and every $r\geq 1$, there is an $\varepsilon>0$ such that if $\phi/L$ is a Drinfeld module of rank $r$ and $x\in\phi(L)$ is non-torsion, then

$$
\hat{h}_\phi(x)\geq \varepsilon\max\{h(j_\phi),\deg(\mathscr{D}_{\phi/L})\}.
$$

This is a conjectural lower bound for canonical heights that strengthens bounds depending only on the number of places of bad reduction. The paper motivates it by analogy with conjectures of Lang and Silverman for elliptic curves; its status is not resolved in the supplied context.
324243.title: Lang–Silverman conjecture for Drinfeld modules

326946.stmt:
Let $\alpha$ be an algebraic number of degree $d\geq 3$ over $\mathbf{Q}$, let $K=\mathbf{Q}(\alpha)$, and let $\mathbf{Z}_K^\times$ be the group of units of $K$. For a unit $\varepsilon\in\mathbf{Z}_K^\times$ with $\delta=[\mathbf{Q}(\alpha\varepsilon):\mathbf{Q}]\geq 3$, let $f_\varepsilon(X)$ be the irreducible polynomial of $\alpha\varepsilon$ over $\mathbf{Z}$ with positive leading coefficient, and define

$$
F_\varepsilon(X,Y)=Y^\delta f_\varepsilon(X/Y)\in\mathbf{Z}[X,Y].
$$

Here $\mathrm{h}(\alpha\varepsilon)$ denotes the height of $\alpha\varepsilon$. **Effective boundedness conjecture.** There exists an effectively computable constant $\kappa_1>0$, depending only on $\alpha$, such that for every $m\geq 2$, each solution $(x,y,\varepsilon)\in\mathbf{Z}^2\times\mathbf{Z}_K^\times$ of

$$
|F_\varepsilon(x,y)|\leq m
$$

with $xy\neq 0$ and $[\mathbf{Q}(\alpha\varepsilon):\mathbf{Q}]\geq 3$ satisfies

$$
\max\{|x|,|y|,e^{\mathrm{h}(\alpha\varepsilon)}\}\leq m^{\kappa_1}.
$$

The conjecture seeks an effective uniform bound for both the integer variables and the height of the varying algebraic parameter in these families of Thue inequalities; the paper establishes such bounds only after restricting the units under consideration, so the full assertion remains open in the supplied text.
326946.title: Effective boundedness conjecture for parametrized Thue inequalities

332023.stmt:
Let $N\ge 3$. For each weight $w\ge 1$, let $\operatorname{CMZV}_{w,N}$, $\operatorname{FCV}_{w,N}$, and $\operatorname{SCV}_{w,N}$ be the $\mathbb{Q}(\mathcal{G}_N)$-spaces generated by colored multiple zeta values, finite colored multiple zeta values, and symmetrized colored multiple zeta values, respectively. Set $\widetilde{\operatorname{SCV}}_{0,N}:=\mathbb{Q}(\mathcal{G}_N)$ and

$$
\widetilde{\operatorname{SCV}}_{w,N}:=\operatorname{SCV}_{w,N}+2\pi i\,\operatorname{SCV}_{w-1,N}
$$

for $w\ge 1$. **The SCV–FCV comparison conjecture.** For every $N\ge 3$ and $w\ge 1$,

$$
\widetilde{\operatorname{SCV}}_{w,N}=\operatorname{CMZV}_{w,N}
$$

as vector spaces over $\mathbb{Q}(\xi_N)$, and there is a $\mathbb{Q}(\mathcal{G}_N)$-algebra isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{FCV}_{w,N}\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}\frac{\operatorname{CMZV}_{w,N}}{2\pi i\,\operatorname{CMZV}_{w-1,N}},\qquad \zeta_{\mathcal{A}(N)}(\mathbf{s};\boldsymbol{\eta})\longmapsto\zeta_{\sha}^{\operatorname{Sy}}(\mathbf{s};\boldsymbol{\eta}).
$$

This conjecture proposes that symmetrized colored multiple zeta values generate the same spaces as colored multiple zeta values after adjoining the $2\pi i$-correction, and that finite colored multiple zeta values realize the corresponding quotient. The analogous level-$1$ result for part (i) has been proved by Yasuda, but the stated level-$N\ge3$ comparison remains unresolved.
332023.title: The SCV–FCV comparison conjecture

334069.stmt:
Let $b_1>\cdots>b_f$, let $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,\dots,m_f)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^f$, and set

$$
\mathcal{E}^{{\bf b};\mathbf{m}}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^f\mathcal{O}(b_i)^{m_i}.
$$

Let $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ be an $l$-tuple of partitions of $n$, let $S_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$ be its stabilizer in $\mathfrak{S}_l$, and let $\mathcal{P}_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$ be the product of partition sets determined by the multiplicities of its distinct coordinates. For $\boldsymbol{\lambda}\in\mathcal{P}_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$, let $D$ be a reduced divisor compatible with $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$, and let $\mathcal{A}^{{\mathcal{E}^{{\bf b};\mathbf{m}}}}_{\boldsymbol{\mu},\boldsymbol{\lambda},D}(q)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of geometrically indecomposable parabolic structures of the prescribed types.

**Deligne's conjecture.** There exists a polynomial $A^{{\bf b};\mathbf{m}}_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}(t)\in\mathcal{C}h(S_{\boldsymbol{\mu}})[t]$, with coefficients in the positive cone $\mathcal{C}h(S_{\boldsymbol{\mu}})^+$, such that for every finite field $k=\mathbb{F}_q$, every $\boldsymbol{\lambda}\in\mathcal{P}_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$, and every compatible reduced divisor $D$, one has

$$
\mathcal{A}^{{\mathcal{E}^{{\bf b};\mathbf{m}}}}_{\boldsymbol{\mu},\boldsymbol{\lambda},D}(q)=A^{{\bf b};\mathbf{m}}_{\boldsymbol{\mu},w}(q),
$$

for any $w\in S_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$ of cycle type $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$.

The conjecture strengthens ordinary polynomiality by packaging the counts as evaluations of a character-valued polynomial. It is attributed in the source to Deligne and is proved there when $n=2$.
334069.title: Deligne's character-valued polynomiality conjecture for parabolic-bundle counts

338937.stmt:
Let $\mathcal{K}^n$ be the family of full-dimensional convex compact sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $\mathcal{K}^n_o$ denote the $o$-symmetric members. For $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$, define its diameter by $\mathrm{D}(K)=\max\{\|x-y\|:x,y\in K\}$ and its isodiametric quotient by

$$
\operatorname{idq}(K)=\frac{\mathrm{vol}(K)}{\mathrm{D}(K)^n}.
$$

A regular simplex and a regular crosspolytope are the corresponding standard comparison bodies.

**Makai Jr.'s conjecture.** For every $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$ there is a linear transformation $A\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that

$$
\operatorname{idq}(AK)\geq\frac{\sqrt{n+1}}{n!\,2^{\frac n2}},
$$

with equality if and only if $AK$ is a regular simplex. If $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_o$, then there is an $A\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that

$$
\operatorname{idq}(AK)\geq\frac1{n!},
$$

with equality if and only if $AK$ is a regular crosspolytope.

The conjecture concerns the reverse isodiametric problem and is motivated by applications to the minimal density of non-separable lattice arrangements of convex bodies. It is open for dimensions $n\geq3$, while the reverse isodiametric problem is solved in the plane.
338937.title: Makai Jr.'s reverse isodiametric conjecture

340221.stmt:
Let $\operatorname{RM}$ be the random model, with a realisation determined by the shifts $a$ and factors $\rho_k(n+a)$, and let $\pi_{\operatorname{RM}}(x)$ be its counting function. Let $\operatorname{Ri}(x)$ be the Riemann prime-counting function. A realisation belongs to the constrained model $\operatorname{RM}_c$ only if

$$
\prod_{k=0}^{\pi(\sqrt n)}\rho_k(n+a)\leq n
$$

for every relevant value of $n$. **Equivalent RH conjecture.** If a realisation of the RM satisfies

$$
\left|\pi_{\operatorname{RM}}(x)-\operatorname{Ri}(x)\right|^2\neq O\left(x(\log x)^2\right),
$$

then there exists at least one value of $n$ such that

$$
\prod_{k=0}^{\pi(\sqrt n)}\rho_k(n+a)>n.
$$

Thus, any realisation violating the stated error bound is not an element of $\operatorname{RM}_c$. The source presents this as an equivalent formulation related to the Riemann hypothesis, but supplies no proof or resolution.
340221.title: Equivalent Riemann hypothesis conjecture for the constrained random model

346153.stmt:
Let $p_1,\dots,p_k$ be $k\geq 2$ different odd prime numbers. For each $i\in\\{1,\dots,k\\}$, set

$$
B_i=\\{0,\dots,(p_i-1)/2\\}.
$$

Define

$$
s=\sum_{i=1}^k\frac{\log\\#B_i}{\log p_i}=\sum_{i=1}^k\frac{\log(p_i+1)-\log 2}{\log p_i}.
$$

Here $N_{p_1,\dots,p_k}^{B_1,\dots,B_k}$ denotes the set of nonnegative integers whose base-$p_i$ expansions use only digits from $B_i$ for every $i$. **Restricted-digit counting conjecture.** If $s\in(k-1,k)$, then for every $\epsilon>0$ there is a constant $C_\epsilon>1$ such that

$$
C_\epsilon^{-1}N^{s-(k-1)-\epsilon}\leq\\#\left(N_{p_1,\dots,p_k}^{B_1,\dots,B_k}\cap[1,N]\right)\leq C_\epsilon N^{s-(k-1)+\epsilon}
$$

for all integers $N\geq2$. If $s<k-1$, then $N_{p_1,\dots,p_k}^{B_1,\dots,B_k}$ is finite. The upper bound is known under Schanuel's conjecture, while the lower bound and finiteness assertion remain open; the claim is related to Furstenberg-type intersection problems.
346153.title: Furstenberg-type restricted-digit counting conjecture

347791.stmt:
Let $\mathcal{F}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{F}_{2d}$ be finite families of convex sets in $\mathds{R}^d$. If $\bigcap_{i=1}^{2d}F_i$ has diameter greater than or equal to $1$ for every $2d$-tuple $(F_i)_{i=1}^{2d}$ with $F_i\in\mathcal{F}_i$, then there exists an index $k\in[2d]$ such that $\bigcap\mathcal{F}_k$ has diameter greater than or equal to $c d^{-1/2}$, for some absolute constant $c$.

**Colorful Bárány–Katchalski–Pach conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, there is an index $k\in[2d]$ whose entire family has intersection of diameter at least $c d^{-1/2}$, for some absolute constant $c$.

This is the colorful analogue of the Bárány–Katchalski–Pach diameter conjecture, with each family viewed as a color class. The source postulates this extension after proving a related colorful fractional theorem; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.
347791.title: Colorful Bárány–Katchalski–Pach diameter conjecture

349042.stmt:
Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $p_1$ be a prime greater than $k+1$. For each index $\boldsymbol{k}$, let $H_{p-1}(\boldsymbol{k})$ be the multiple harmonic sum, and let $c_{\boldsymbol{k}}$ be a finite set of rational coefficients indexed by indices of weight $k$. Suppose

$$
\sum_{\operatorname{wt}(\boldsymbol{k})=k}c_{\boldsymbol{k}}H_{p-1}(\boldsymbol{k})\equiv0\pmod p
$$

for all primes $p\ge p_1$. **Rosen's lifting conjecture.** For each $n\ge2$, there exists a prime $p_n$ and a finite set of rational numbers $c_{\boldsymbol{k}}^{(l)}$, indexed by $1\le l\le n-1$ and indices of weight $k+l$, such that $p_n\ge p_{n-1}$ and

$$
\sum_{\operatorname{wt}(\boldsymbol{k})=k}c_{\boldsymbol{k}}H_{p-1}(\boldsymbol{k})+\sum_{l=1}^{n-1}p^l\sum_{\operatorname{wt}(\boldsymbol{k})=k+l}c_{\boldsymbol{k}}^{(l)}H_{p-1}(\boldsymbol{k})\equiv0\pmod {p^n}
$$

for all primes $p\ge p_n$. This is a lifting principle: a congruence modulo $p$ should admit coefficient corrections that lift it to every higher power of $p$. The supplied text presents it as a version of Rosen's lifting conjecture and gives no resolution status.
349042.title: Rosen's lifting conjecture for multiple harmonic sums

349943.stmt: Let $\Gamma$ be a quiver, let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field, and suppose that for every $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^n$ there is a polynomial $r(\alpha,q)\in\mathbb{Z}[q]$ such that $|\operatorname{Rep}(\alpha,\mathbb{F}_{q^d})_\mathcal{R}|=r(\alpha,q^d)$ for every $d\geq 1$, where $\operatorname{Rep}(\alpha,\mathbb{F}_q)_\mathcal{R}$ denotes the representations of dimension $\alpha$ respecting the relations $\mathcal{R}$ nilpotently. Let $A(\alpha,q)$ be the polynomial counting isomorphism classes of absolutely indecomposable representations of dimension $\alpha$. **Non-negativity conjecture.** All coefficients of $A(\alpha,q)$ are non-negative integers. The assertion concerns the positivity of the counting polynomials arising from quivers with nilpotent relations. The supplied context does not state whether this conjecture has been proved or disproved.
349943.title: Non-negativity conjecture for absolutely indecomposable representation polynomials

350668.stmt:
Let $K$ be a number field or a one-dimensional function field of characteristic zero, and let $n\ge 3$. Let $[Z_1:\cdots:Z_n]$ be the standard homogeneous coordinates on $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}(K)$, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be the hyperplane given by

$$
Z_1+\dots+Z_n=0.
$$

For $P=(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in\mathbb{P}^{n-1}(K)$ with nonzero coordinates, let $h(P)$ be the height and $\operatorname{rad}(P)$ the radical defined in the source. **The $abcd$-conjecture.** For any $\epsilon>0$, there is a proper Zariski closed subset $\mathcal{Z}=\mathcal{Z}(K,\epsilon,n)\subsetneq\mathcal{H}$ and a constant $C_{K,\mathcal{Z},\epsilon,n}$ such that for all $P=(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{Z}$ with $z_1,\dots,z_n\in K^*$, we have

$$
h(P)<(1+\epsilon)\operatorname{rad}(P)+C_{K,\mathcal{Z},\epsilon,n}.
$$

This generalizes the $abc$-conjecture, which corresponds to $n=3$, and is used in the source to prove results on uniform boundedness and dynamical Lang-type statements. The source gives no resolution status for this formulation.
350668.title: The $abcd$-conjecture

360178.title: The classification conjecture for maximal subgroups containing the cyclic factor

361816.stmt:
Let $G$ be a non-abelian finite simple group. A **non-trivial conjugacy class** is a conjugacy class other than the identity class. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\geq 2$, consider the product of $n$ non-trivial conjugacy classes of $G$.

**Arad–Herzog conjecture.** This product is not a conjugacy class.

The conjecture generalizes the original assertion of Z. Arad and M. Herzog for the product of two classes. It has been confirmed for several families of finite simple groups, including sporadic simple groups, and for squares of a conjugacy class; the general case remains open.
361816.title: Arad–Herzog conjecture on products of non-trivial conjugacy classes

368351.stmt: For a nonnegative integer $n$, an MC-circle is a largest circle enclosing exactly $n$ lattice points in its interior, and $R_n$ is its radius; an integer is MC if it is maximally circlable and non-MC otherwise. A lattice circle is a circle with at least three lattice points on its circumference. For $n\ne6$, let $\rho_n$ be the radius of the largest $n$-enclosing lattice circle when one exists, and set $\rho_n=0$ otherwise; a strong MC number is an MC number immediately followed by a non-MC number. **MC-circle distribution conjectures.** The following assertions hold: for MC numbers $k<\ell$, $R_k<R_\ell$; every non-MC $n\ne6$ has a largest $n$-enclosing lattice circle; the values in $\{\rho_n\}_{n\ge0}$ are pairwise distinct; there are arbitrarily long consecutive sequences of MC numbers and of non-MC numbers; the density of MC numbers is greater than $80\%$, while that of non-MC numbers is positive and less than $20\%$; strong MC numbers are infinite and have positive density among MC numbers; every MC-circle of a strong MC number has at least six lattice points on its circumference; the stated majority, minority, and percentage claims about mirror symmetries and axes of symmetry in items (10)--(19) hold exactly as listed in the source. These claims are extrapolated from computations for $n<1100$ and remain unresolved in the paper.
368351.title: Conjectures on radii, densities, and symmetries of maximally circlable circles

371095.stmt:
Let $\rho\in M_3\otimes M_n$ be an absolutely PPT state with $n\geq 2$, and let $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{3n}$ be its eigenvalues. **Maximum-purity conjecture.** The maximum purity of absolutely PPT states is

$$
\begin{cases}
\frac{4}{9n} &\text{if } n\equiv 0\pmod 4,\\
\frac{36n+8}{(9n+1)^2} &\text{if } n\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\
\frac{36n+16}{(9n+2)^2} &\text{if } n\equiv 2\pmod 4,\\
\frac{36n-8}{(9n-1)^2} &\text{if } n\equiv 3\pmod 4.
\end{cases}
$$

Moreover, the maximum is attained when

$$
\begin{cases}
\lambda_1=\cdots=\lambda_{\frac{3n}{4}}=\frac2{3n},\quad \lambda_{\frac{3n}{4}+1}=\cdots=\lambda_{3n}=\frac2{9n} &\text{if } n\equiv 0\pmod 4,\\
\lambda_1=\cdots=\lambda_{\frac{3n+1}{4}}=\frac6{9n+1},\quad \lambda_{\frac{3n+5}{4}}=\cdots=\lambda_{3n}=\frac2{9n+1} &\text{if } n\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\
\lambda_1=\cdots=\lambda_{\frac{3n+2}{4}}=\frac6{9n+2},\quad \lambda_{\frac{3n+6}{4}}=\cdots=\lambda_{3n}=\frac2{9n+2} &\text{if } n\equiv 2\pmod 4,\\
\lambda_1=\cdots=\lambda_{\frac{3n-1}{4}}=\frac6{9n-1},\quad \lambda_{\frac{3n+3}{4}}=\cdots=\lambda_{3n}=\frac2{9n-1} &\text{if } n\equiv 3\pmod 4.
\end{cases}
$$

The formulas are motivated by numerical estimates, which become smaller than the conjectured values as the dimension increases; the conjecture remains open.
371095.title: Conjectured maximum purity of absolutely PPT qutrit-qudit states

378950.stmt:
Let $G$ be a group such that the classifying space for proper $G$-actions, $\underline{E}G$, has a finite model. Let $A_{\operatorname{ho}}(G)=\pi_G^0(\underline{E}G)$, let ${\mathbf I}_G=\ker(\epsilon^G)$ be the augmentation ideal, and let $X$ be a finite proper $G$-$CW$-complex. Write $\pi_G^n(X)\widehat{_{\mathbf I_G}}$ for the ${\mathbf I}_G$-adic completion of the $A_{\operatorname{ho}}(G)$-module $\pi_G^n(X)$. **Segal Conjecture for infinite groups.** There is an isomorphism

$$
\pi_s^n(EG\times_GX)\xrightarrow{\cong}\pi_G^n(X)\widehat{_{\mathbf I_G}}.
$$

In particular, for all $n\in{\mathbb Z}$,

$$
\pi_s^n(BG)\xrightarrow{\cong}\pi_G^n(\underline{E}G)\widehat{_{\mathbf I_G}};
$$

and for $n=0$,

$$
\pi_s^0(BG)\xrightarrow{\cong}A_{\operatorname{ho}}(G)\widehat{_{\mathbf I_G}}.
$$

This is the proposed completion theorem extending the classical Segal conjecture from finite groups to groups with finite models for $\underline{E}G$; the supplied text gives no resolution.
378950.title: Segal Conjecture for infinite groups

380396.stmt:
Let $Y$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over the finite field $\mathbb F_q$, let $D$ be an effective divisor on $Y$, and let $N$ be a positive integer. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathbb F_q}$ be the tensor category used in the source, and let $\phi_n$ denote its numerical realization over $\mathbb Q$.

**Algebra conjecture for motivic local systems.** There exists a commutative associative unital algebra $A=A_{Y,D,N}$ in $\mathcal C_{\mathbb F_q}$ such that, for every $n\ge 1$, $\phi_n(A)$ is semisimple over $\mathbb Q$, and for every prime $l$ with $(l,q)=1$ there is a bijection

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q\text{-alg}}(\phi_n(A),\overline{\mathbb Q})
$$

with the elements of $\operatorname{IrrRep}^{\mathrm{mot,geom}}_{Y\times_{\mathbb F_q}\mathbb F_{q^n},N}$ whose ramification divisor is $D$. The bijection is equivariant for the natural action of ${\operatorname{Gal}}(\overline{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q)\times\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$.

This conjecture proposes a finite-dimensional algebra whose geometric points parameterize motivic local systems with prescribed ramification. It would organize the expected independence from $l$ and the Galois and cyclic symmetries, but is not established in the source.
380396.title: The algebra conjecture for parameterizing motivic local systems

380398.stmt:
Let $\mathcal C_{\mathbb F_p}$ be the tensor category of the source, let $\mathcal A'$ be its proposed complex representation-theoretic analogue, and let $({\mathcal A}')^{\mathrm{kar}}$ be the Karoubi closure of $\mathcal A'$. Let $\phi_n$ and $\phi_n^{\mathcal A'}$ be the corresponding realization functors, and let $\operatorname{Fr}_X$ denote the Frobenius element of an object $X$.

**Tensor-functor realization conjecture.** For every prime $p$ there exists a tensor functor

$$
\Phi_p:\mathcal C_{\mathbb F_p}\to({\mathcal A}')^{\mathrm{kar}}
$$

and, for every $n\ge 1$, an isomorphism of tensor functors

$$
\operatorname{iso}_{n,p}:\phi_n^{\mathcal A'}\circ\Phi_p\simeq i_{\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb Q}\to\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb C}}\circ\phi_n,
$$

where $i_{\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb Q}\to\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbb C}}$ is the scalar-extension embedding. Moreover, for every $X\in\mathcal C_{\mathbb F_p}$, $\Phi_p$ maps $\operatorname{Fr}_X$ to $\operatorname{Fr}_{\Phi_p(X)}$.

This is the paper's Master Conjecture: it seeks a tensor realization of the finite-field motivic category inside a representation-theoretic category while preserving all numerical realizations and Frobenius elements. It is open in the source.
380398.title: The tensor-functor realization conjecture for finite-field motives

380771.stmt:
Let a **straight-line program** for a polynomial in one variable be a list

$$
s_0=1,\quad s_1=x,\quad s_2,\ldots,s_{\tau},
$$

where each $s_i$, for $i\geq 2$, is one of $s_j+s_k$, $s_j-s_k$, or $s_js_k$ for some $j,k<i$. For $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$, let $\tau(f)$ be the least length of a straight-line program computing $f$, and let $n(f)$ denote the number of distinct integer zeros of $f$. **Integer-zero bound conjecture.** There is a constant $a>0$ such that, for every univariate polynomial $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$,

$$
n(f)<\tau(f)^a.
$$

Such a bound would connect the arithmetic complexity of straight-line programs with the number of integer roots and is presented in the context of complexity over $\mathbb C$ and the separation of polynomial-time and nondeterministic polynomial-time computation.
380771.title: The polynomial bound on integer zeros of straight-line computable polynomials

381331.stmt:
Let $\Delta$ be a triangle with vertices at $(0,0)$, $\mathbf P_1=(a_1,b_1)$, and $\mathbf P_2=(a_2,b_2)$. Assume the hypotheses on the prime $p$ from the main theorem. Let $\mathrm{NP}(f,\chi)_C$ denote the corresponding Newton polygon for a polynomial $f(x_1,x_2)$ whose Newton polytope is the convex hull $\Delta$, and let $\mathrm{IHP}(\Delta)$ be the associated infinite Hodge polygon. **Folklore conjecture.** In the moduli space of all such polynomials, there exists an open dense subspace over which, for every finite character $\chi$, every integer $k\geq 1$, and every integer $i_k$ satisfying $0\leq i_k\leq \mathbbm x_k'-\mathbbm x_k$, the Newton polygon agrees with the infinite Hodge polygon at

$$
x=\mathbbm x_k+i_k.
$$

The claim concerns generic polynomials with triangular Newton polytope and would provide the coincidence needed to apply the paper's main theorem. The supplied context describes it as a folklore conjecture and gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
381331.title: Folklore generic Newton polygon conjecture for triangular exponential sums
